_comment: The offer ladder. Every rung is derived from something already built or
already known - nothing here needs a new skill acquired first.
Ladder logic: the cheap digital rungs earn while nobody is awake but
convert slowly; the service rungs pay properly but consume evenings.
The subscription rung is the only one that makes revenue 'constant'.
Run `revenue plan` to see which mix actually closes the gap.

offers.name: Section & Chapter Event Automation Kit
offers.description: The working pattern behind the IEEE Houston toolkit, packaged: the two-phase propose/publish design, the approval gate, the vTools/eNotice/WordPress field maps, the CLAUDE.md that makes an agent safe to hand a live account. Sold to the ~340 IEEE sections and several thousand chapters whose officers do this by hand.

offers.name: Agentic Ops Playbook: automating systems with no API
offers.description: The transferable version. How to put an agent in front of a legacy browser-bound system safely: calibration over hardcoded selectors, propose/publish phase separation, idempotent retries, refusing to act on missing data. Audience is ops and platform engineers, not IEEE.

offers.name: Automation Teardown (90 minutes, recorded)
offers.description: Live session on one manual workflow, followed by a written automation plan: what to automate, what to leave alone, the approval gates it needs, and the order to build it in. Caps at four a month because it costs three real hours each.

offers.name: Managed Section Ops (per section, monthly)
offers.description: The toolkit run as a service for one section or chapter: events proposed, drafts sent for approval, published on a yes, post-event reports filed. Approval always stays with the officer. This is the rung that turns lumpy income into constant income.
